title: Hillel and the Man on One Foot
text:
The Talmud tells of a gentile who came to the great teacher Shammai with a challenge. "Convert me," he said, "on condition that you teach me the whole Torah while I stand on one foot."

Shammai was a strict man and took this as mockery. He pushed the man away with the builder's measuring rod he was holding.

The man then went to Hillel and made the same demand. Hillel did not get angry. He accepted him and said, "What is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow. That is the whole Torah. The rest is commentary. Now go and learn it."

The Talmud places this story among several in which impatient or provocative would-be converts were sent away by Shammai and received by Hillel. Later, it says, these converts met and agreed that Shammai's strictness had nearly driven them from the world, while Hillel's patience had brought them under the wings of the divine presence.
lesson: A hard question deserves a patient answer. And when you are unsure how to treat someone, start with what you would not want done to you.
